Topics · One God, one message

Is the true God beyond what people worship?

The Kena, an Upanishad, looks beyond what is worshipped here. The Quran asks with it: who creates, who hears?

Part 1 of 3

﴿أَفَمَن يَخْلُقُ كَمَن لَّا يَخْلُقُ ۗ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Then is He who creates like one who does not create? So will you not be reminded?

Quran · An-Nahl 16:17

The Kena looks beyond what people worship here, to what stands behind all hearing and seeing. A question the Quran also asks looks the same way: can one who makes be compared with one who makes nothing? Both lift the eye to the One who brings all things into being. Ask it quietly, of your own practice only, and see where the Kena's line falls for you.

A question for you

When you read the Kena's line, what do you take it to set aside?

If you sayAny form the mind can hold
ThenThat is close to the Quran's own thought: what is held in the mind or the hands is a thing among things. The next verses ask what such things can do.
If you sayOnly the wrong attitude toward a form, not the form itself
ThenMany teachers in your tradition read it so: the image is a doorway, not the destination. The next verses ask what lies at the end of the call.
If you sayI read it differently
ThenThen hold your reading beside these verses. The Kena opens by asking who stands behind all hearing and seeing, and the next verses ask who truly answers.

Part 2 of 3

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ضُرِبَ مَثَلٌ فَٱسْتَمِعُوا۟ لَهُۥٓ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَن يَخْلُقُوا۟ ذُبَابًا وَلَوِ ٱجْتَمَعُوا۟ لَهُۥ ۖ وَإِن يَسْلُبْهُمُ ٱلذُّبَابُ شَيْـًٔا لَّا يَسْتَنقِذُوهُ مِنْهُ ۚ ضَعُفَ ٱلطَّالِبُ وَٱلْمَطْلُوبُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O people, an example is presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke besides Allāh will never create [as much as] a fly, even if they gathered together for it [i.e., that purpose]. And if the fly should steal from them a [tiny] thing, they could not recover it from him. Weak are the pursuer and pursued.[943]

Translator's notes

[943] A comparison is made here to the worshipper of a false deity and that which he worships.

Quran · Al-Hajj 22:73

Translation

The God who made the world and all things in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands. He isn’t served by men’s hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself gives to all life and breath and all things.

Original · Ancient Greek

ὁ θεὸς ὁ ποιήσας τὸν κόσμον καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ, οὗτος οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς ὑπάρχων κύριος οὐκ ἐν χειροποιήτοις ναοῖς κατοικεῖ οὐδὲ ὑπὸ χειρῶν ἀνθρωπίνων θεραπεύεται προσδεόμενός τινος, αὐτὸς διδοὺς πᾶσι ζωὴν καὶ πνοὴν καὶ τὰ πάντα·

Acts · 17:24-25

World English Bible

Here the Quran puts the question so anyone can weigh it. What is called on in place of the One cannot create even a fly, it says, though all of them gather for it, and if a fly takes something from them they cannot get it back. The verse names no one's practice. It sets two measures: to create and to rescue. Then it leaves the measure in your hands.

A question for you

In your hardest hour, what did you most need from the one you called on?

If you sayTo hear me
ThenHearing is the next subject: the next verse speaks of who answers.
If you sayTo rescue me
ThenThat is one of the two measures in the verse: whatever rescues must be able to take back what is taken.
If you sayTo be with me
ThenThat is a deep need, and the Quran meets it: the One is near. The next verse speaks of who answers.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا۟ لِى وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِى لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when My servants ask you, [O Muḥammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:186

Translation

Yahweh is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.

Original · Hebrew

קָר֣וֹב יְ֭הוָה לְכָל־קֹרְאָ֑יו לְכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁ֖ר יִקְרָאֻ֣הוּ בֶאֱמֶֽת׃

the Psalms · 145:18

World English Bible

The verse adds a third measure, in God's own voice: He is near, and He answers the one who calls. That leaves each person something to weigh alone: who truly answers a call? The Kena's own story meets it here: the gods learn that their power comes from what stands behind them.

A question for you

If a call is to be answered at all, which of these would have to be true of the one who answers?

If you sayThat it hears everything, everywhere
ThenThat agrees with this verse: the One who answers is near to whoever calls. And the Kena says the real lies beyond what is worshipped here.
If you sayThat it is greater than anything inside the world
ThenThat agrees with the Kena itself: the source of everything cannot be a part of it. And the verse adds that this same One is near.
If you sayI do not know yet
ThenAn honest answer. The last step asks you to put it in your own words, as far as you know it now.

The same in the other books
